A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mixture of Horizons in Action Chunking. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original LIBERO and RoboTwin evaluations, ablations, dynamic-inference measurements and real-robot experiments, with additional analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds RoboCasa evaluations, StarVLA experiments, towel folding and further controlled analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same horizon truncation and masking, shared action transformer, linear gating, training losses and consensus-based dynamic inference. StarVLA is an additional application of the existing procedure; no MoH algorithm change is documented.

E1.justification: v2 retains LIBERO, seven RoboTwin tasks and the three original real-world tasks, while adding five RoboCasa household tasks and diagonal towel folding. These additions extend evaluation environments and introduce deformable-object manipulation.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds StarVLA and its MoH variant while retaining the existing comparators, including GR00T-N1. New Table 5 evaluates CogACT's Adaptive Temporal Ensemble, both alone and combined with MoH, on π0 and π0.5. These introduce a distinct backbone comparison and a substantive competing fusion strategy.

E3.justification: New protocols include RoboCasa training with 200 demonstrations per task, 10-step execution and 150 evaluation rollouts per task, plus towel folding with 40 demonstrations and 20 rollouts. Additional analyses vary maximum horizon with ten branches fixed and measure first-five-action L1 error on LIBERO training data. The original experiments' stated protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds an identical-horizon ensemble control, maximum-horizon sensitivity analysis, per-step action-error analysis, task-dependent gating statistics and within-rollout threshold analysis (Table 4 and Tables 8–11). These investigate alternative explanations and mechanisms beyond v1's retained density, fusion and balance-loss ablations. Existing failure cases are relocated, not newly added.

E5.justification: RoboCasa results in v2 Table 2 introduce means and standard deviations across three random seeds. This uncertainty-reporting practice is absent from v1, but remains limited to the new benchmark; the retained LIBERO setup still specifies one training run with a fixed seed.

E6.justification: Existing headline results, including 99.0% LIBERO success, are retained. New comparisons report baseline versus MoH averages of 95.9% versus 97.0% for StarVLA and 28.0% versus 31.4% on RoboCasa, plus 75% versus 90% for towel folding. v2 also adds ensemble, ATE, horizon-sensitivity, action-error, gating and threshold results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(17) retain the same mathematical definitions, objectives and derivations. No theorem, proof or revised formal assumption is introduced; the added mechanism and threshold discussions are empirical or conceptual.

C1.justification: The three central contributions remain the horizon trade-off, plug-and-play MoH and consensus-based dynamic inference. The 99% LIBERO and 2.5× throughput claims remain; removing the former from the abstract does not remove it from the introduction and conclusion. Additional experiments support the existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations distinguishing horizon diversity from generic ensembling, attributes ATE degradation to cumulative drift, and interprets action errors and gating shifts. Appendices C and H discuss proposed pretraining use and threshold rationale. Section 4.4 explicitly clarifies that throughput measures executed actions per predicted chunk, rather than wall-clock speed.

D1.justification: v2 documents StarVLA's Qwen3-VL backbone and setup details for the added experiments. However, it removes v1's project link and the maximum-gradient-norm value of 1.0 from the hyperparameter table. These are documentation changes; they do not establish code withdrawal or changed gradient clipping.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Qwen3-VL, StarVLA, RoboCasa365 and SimpleVLA-RL, and explicitly distinguishes MoH's within-planning-step horizon fusion from CogACT's temporal ensembling. The broader related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and real-world discussion are condensed, subsection headings are simplified, and latency, gating statistics and detailed rollout discussion move into dedicated appendix sections. Motivation and discussion passages are added, but the introduction and method narrative remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts an ICML layout with running headers and single-column appendices, adds multiple result tables, and redesigns Table 1 with shading and improvement annotations. Latency and gating plots move to the appendix; the main rollout figure is shortened and annotated while its full sequence remains in the appendix.

improvement.justification: The additional backbone and harder-benchmark evaluations strengthen generality, while identical-horizon and ATE controls address important alternative explanations left unresolved in v1. RoboCasa uncertainty reporting and the explicit throughput definition improve evidential transparency. These substantial gains outweigh the limited loss of reproducibility information from removing the project link and gradient-clipping disclosure.
